title: Picou's arrangements and the 1930-32 band
summary: Picou rearranged records; Robinson hums the trombone ending for the recorder; this was his last band, 1930-32.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He was on the way to George Gano. He said he had to be there. He was the one to take him some papers and try some numbers with him. So he was in a hurry to run over. He would have stopped there. Did Piku have many other pieces that he wrote that you know of in those days? Did he have many other numbers by him? Or was that the only one that you remember that he wrote?
Oh, he rearranged a couple of records. Oh, that could come from me. He rearranged some records.

I wonder if you don't mind, due to that noise there with all of those cars, I'm not sure that it picked up that tune very well. And I'd like to be able to hear it sometime. If you don't mind, we can point this maybe a little bit, get it up a little closer to you. And if you don't mind humming it, I don't like to make it do all that over again. But I'm not sure it's on there real clear. If you don't mind that tune again of Piku's and I'll hold this mic up a little closer to you.
You see that's why he makes the run on the planet. That was your trombone part at the end. Sort of like a break at the end. Yeah, that's the break you used to get at the end.
Did they all come in for one final note there? When I make...
Just went up... That was the last.
I think I'll leave this mic sit right up here and it'll pick up. You don't have to face it there. It'll pick you up alright. Yeah. It's a little better there.
What year was that when you were playing that with Piku?
I'll give it that. That was about 19... Between 30 and 32.
That was your last band that you played in.
